topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by outlining the framework of cancer evolution and the intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Clonal Evolution and Epigenetic Alterations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cell-intrinsic advantages during early tumorigenesis are acquired through both genetic clonal selection and epigenetic reprogramming.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Cancer Stem Cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the evidence for a cellular hierarchy in cancer and demonstrate that malignancies frequently arise from tissue-specific stem cells possessing intrinsic self-renewal capacity.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and Inflammatory Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate that extrinsic inflammatory signals and stromal support are required alongside mutations to permit tumor initiation, progression, and maintenance.

topics.label: Experimental and Computational Methods for Studying Tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the single-cell sequencing and spatial omics technologies used to investigate tumor evolution and microenvironmental interactions in the laboratory.

topics.label: Multifactorial Model of Cancer Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes how genetic alterations, cellular stemness, and microenvironmental factors integrate into a unified evolutionary model of cancer development.

topics.label: Closing Framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapy.
